## Global change impacts Earth's systems
<hr>
<br/>
<br/>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 50%;">

**Many of Earth's system's interact at the ecosystem level**

<br/>

**Ecosystem = **

<br/>

**A change in just one <span style="color:blue">*biotic*</span> or <span style="color:blue">*abiotic*</span> factor can alter complex relationships and have large scale consequences**

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:220px; LEFT:575px; WIDTH:450px; HEIGHT:450px" SRC="images/earthsystems.png">

## In ecosystems, abiotic and biotic processes interact
<hr>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 50%;">

**Ecosystems (and higher levels) are regulated by the <span style="color:darkred">flow of energy</span> and the <span style="color:darkred">cycling of nutrients</span>**

<br/>

**Life is composed of this <span style="color:blue">energy</span> and <span style="color:blue">matter</span>, which is always on the move**

<br/>

- **Energy from the sun powers communities, ecosystems, biomes, etc**
    + heat flows from hot to cold
    + energy goes on a one-way trip
    
<br/>

- **Matter, including the chemical building blocks of life, cycles around the biosphere**
    + Law of Conservation of Mass

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:200px; LEFT:575px; WIDTH:500px; HEIGHT:450px" SRC="images/energymatter.jpg">

## Energy from the sun flows through food webs
<hr>
**This one way flow is very inefficient. Producers (plants) convert light energy into usable chemical energy. As that energy is consumed (trophic levels) only a fraction is converted to biomass**

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:220px; LEFT:25px; WIDTH:600px; HEIGHT:450px" SRC="images/foodweb.png">

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:240px; LEFT:620px; WIDTH:500px; HEIGHT:350px" SRC="images/cow.jpeg">

## Global change can impact any level of energy flow
<hr>
**Can reduce species biomass and create a less productive system with lower resilience**

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:180px; LEFT:150px; WIDTH:800px; HEIGHT:500px" SRC="images/articfood.jpg">

## Energy flow and efficiency is partially temperature dependent!
<hr>
<span style="color:red">**Projected decrease in energy transfer efficiency is expected to lead to a ~20% decrease in abundance of predators in marine ecosystems**</span>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:220px; LEFT:150px; WIDTH:800px; HEIGHT:450px" SRC="images/tempflow.jpg">

## Why care about Nitrogen?
<hr>
<br/>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 48%;">

**Nitrogen is one of the fundamental building blocks for life on Earth, especially plants**

<br/>

- **Nitrogen is the limiting factor in how productive plant growth can be**
    + via chlorophyll and Rubisco enzyme (15%)
    + producers at bottom of food webs
    + human food security

<br/>

- **Nitrogen is a primary ingredient in fertilizers**

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:220px; LEFT:570px; WIDTH:500px; HEIGHT:375px" SRC="images/plantnitro.png">

## Global change will alter most parts of the nitrogen cycle
<hr>
<span style="color:red">**Not all the nutrients in fertilizers get absorbed by plants and the excess moves its way into rivers, lakes, oceans and groundwater as agricultural runoff**</span>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:215px; LEFT:125px; WIDTH:850px; HEIGHT:450px" SRC="images/reactivenitro.jpg">

## Aquatic dead zones
<hr>

**Eutrophication is when a body of water becomes enriched with phosphorus and nitrogen, causing excessive algae. This leads to negative consequences such as the depletion of dissolved oxygen.**

<br/>
**https://earthobservatory.nasa.gov/images/44677/aquatic-dead-zones**

## Energy and matter movement are goverened by global cycles
<hr>
**<span style="color:purple">CARBON is stored in all parts of the biosphere. One of those storage pools (atmosphere) is the main culprit of climate change. The other storage pools are called carbon sinks.</span>**

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:205px; LEFT:150px; WIDTH:800px; HEIGHT:480px" SRC="images/carbonbiogeo.png">

## Why care about carbon?
<hr>

<div style="float: left; width: 52%;">

**Carbon is in carbon dioxide and methane, both greenhouse gases that trap heat close to Earth**

<br/>

- **Carbon is stored deep earth, plants and oceans for potentially long time scales**
    + keeps carbon out of atmosphere <span style="color:purple">(sinks)</span>
 
<br/>
 
- **Humans are (1) removing carbon from storage pools and (2) preventing carbon from entering storage pools**
    + reducing the carbon sinks

<br/>

**Carbon footprint is used as shorthand for the amount of carbon being emitted by an activity or organization**

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:180px; LEFT:575px; WIDTH:525px; HEIGHT:450px" SRC="images/carbonfootprint.jpg">

## Global change will alter most parts of the carbon cycle
<hr>
<br/>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 40%;">

* **Altering sinks**
    + removing forests
    + digging up fossil fuels
    + thawing frozen soils

<br/>

* **Altering sources**
    + burning fossil fuels
    + ↑ agriculture (livestock)

<br/>

* **Both ↑ C in atmosphere**

</div>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:190px; LEFT:365px; WIDTH:650px; HEIGHT:475px" SRC="images/presentcarbon.jpg">

## Why does global cycling of elements/water matter?
<hr>
<br/>
<br/>
<br/>

<div style="float: left; width: 50%;">

**These cycles interact to regulate the biosphere, including climate &#8594;**

<br/>

**Biogeochemistry is a foundation of biomes: living things adapted to a specific regions  &#8594;**

<br/>

**Ecosystems are the interactions with the biotic and abiotic within those regions**

</div>


<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:200px; LEFT:550px; WIDTH:550px; HEIGHT:400px" SRC="images/biomes.png">

## Biogeochemical provinces in oceans shift...
<hr>

<span style="color:red">**Biogeochemical provinces are dynamic entities that change their spatial extent and position with climate and are expected to be perturbated in the near future by global change**</span>

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:210px; LEFT:150px; WIDTH:800px; HEIGHT:450px" SRC="images/oceanprovince.jpg">

## Are foundations of biomes changing?
<hr>
**A biome is a large geographic area defined by its specific climate and the types of organisms that have adapted to live there. Some biomes are more sensitive/less resilient to change than others**

<IMG STYLE="position:absolute; TOP:200px; LEFT:200px; WIDTH:700px; HEIGHT:500px" SRC="images/surface.jpg">
